about: Dye library (BSD-3-Clause). Spectra, peak wavelengths, extinction coefficients (eps, M^-1 cm^-1, at the absorption peak), quantum yields (qy) and lifetimes come from FPbase (refs: lambert2019) unless 'override' gives a value; fpbase_spectra.json holds what was fetched. Kinetics are per mode. Every number names its source in 'refs'/'notes'; 'estimate' marks a value with no measurement behind it (tune it, then cite).

Modes: dSTORM (bleaching dye: ON at t = 0 for Exp(initialOnSec), then dark; returns at the activation rate; blinks ON Exp(onSec) and bleaches with bleachProb per blink), PALM (photoconversion at the activation rate, then blinks ON Exp(onSec) / dark Exp(offSec), bleachProb per blink; an emissive pre state shines until conversion), DNA-PAINT (persistent site: binding rate k_on x imager concentration, ON Exp(onSec), never bleaches; the free imager adds a uniform background), WideField (always on, bleaches after an exponential photon budget).

dSTORM blocks hold Dempsey et al. 2011 Table 1 (GLOX + 10 mM MEA): detected photons per switching cycle, equilibrium duty cycle, mean switching cycles. tools/gen_dye_library.mjs turns them into onSec / offSec / bleachProb at the reference light path in 'dstormReference' (ON time fixed, so photons per blink scale with the excitation intensity in a simulation).

dstormReference.notes: Dempsey et al. 2011 measured Table 1 at 488 nm (1.2 kW/cm^2), 561 nm (2.2 kW/cm^2) and 647 nm (0.8 kW/cm^2; modelled with the 640 nm line) in TIRF, through ET535/50m, FF01-617/73 and ET700/75m (modelled as ideal band passes), on an EMCCD (QE 0.9 assumed). They found photons per switching cycle largely independent of the laser intensity, because the emission rate and the off-switching rate both depend linearly on it, and the duty cycle about constant (on-switching linear too; Results, 'Dependence of switching properties on light intensity', Supplementary Fig. 32). So a dSTORM dye's ON time, spontaneous dark time and initial ON time scale as 1 / (its excitation rate relative to kExcRef, the rate at this reference); the 405 nm activation adds on top. Exceptions they report (Cy3B photons rising with intensity; fewer switching cycles at high intensity for e.g. ATTO 655) are not modelled.

typicalLabels.notes: Per target (data/specimens.json) and mode: the dye a target gets when its label is 'Typical' (Micro-Manager, the viewer; the engine's <prefix>-dye = -1), and the % of its binding sites labelled when its mode changes or with <prefix>-label-pct = -1. Dyes: the common choices -- Alexa Fluor 647 the best-performing dSTORM dye of Dempsey et al. 2011, mEos3.2 a monomeric photoconvertible FP for PALM fusions (Zhang et al. 2012), an ATTO 655 imager for DNA-PAINT (Schnitzbauer et al. 2017), mEGFP for widefield; typical, not the only choices. Labelling %: estimates (microtubules: % of their 1625 sites/um; DNA-PAINT keeps the pre-issue-16 default; immunolabelling with dSTORM dyes and FP fusions for PALM label a few % of the sites). Nuclear pores (% of the 64 Nup96 sites per pore): the effective labelling efficiencies of Thevathasan et al. 2019 (Fig. 3i): Nup96-SNAP + BG-AF647 58 % (dSTORM), Nup96-mMaple 58 % (PALM; here on mEos3.2, the library's PALM protein); DNA-PAINT 60 %: anti-GFP nanobody docking strands on Nup96-mEGFP, 54.6-68.2 % (Soeller et al. 2025), with a Cy3B imager (the common orange DNA-PAINT imager, Schnitzbauer et al. 2017) so the pores image in a second colour next to the microtubules' ATTO 655; WideField: a homozygous Nup96-mEGFP knock-in tags every copy (100 %, estimate; the dye's fluorescent fraction applies on top).

defaults.notes: each target's preset when its <prefix>-binder option (Micro-Manager CellField.<Target>_Binder) is not set; chosen by the user 2026-10-12 to match the default labels (DNA-PAINT on both targets: microtubules by antibodies with docking strands, pores by Nup96-SNAP with a docking strand). The world model's own default stays Legacy

presets.name: Built-in (before the linkage model)
presets.notes: each structure's numbers before the linkage model (scope/dyes.js LEGACY_LINKAGE, bit for bit): microtubules a rigid 12 nm binder radially from the 12.5 nm lattice plus a 2-5 nm linker (the scale of mikhaylova2015, weber1978; estimate); pores webSMLM's 2-5 nm linker on the Nup96 site, no binder (estimate)

presets.name: Primary + secondary antibody (dye)
presets.notes: Fruh et al. 2021 Table 1, U2OS, AF647 on site-specifically labelled secondaries: dye shell radius 22.5 nm from the microtubule axis, FWHM 16.9 nm. Binder = 22.5 - 12.5 = 10.0 nm; flexibility: a uniform ball's radial profile (1 - x^2/F^2) has FWHM sqrt(2) F, so F = 16.9 / sqrt(2) = 12.0 nm; linker: the dye sits a C5-like linker, about 0.5 nm, from its attachment on the antibody (Results; it adds < 0.1 nm to the shell). Pores: Thevathasan et al. 2019 measured the Nup96 ring radius 64.3 nm with antibodies vs 53.7 nm with SNAP

presets.name: Labelled primary antibody (dye)
presets.notes: Fruh et al. 2021 Table 1, U2OS, AF647 on site-specifically labelled primaries: shell radius 20.2 nm (binder 7.7), FWHM 10.0 nm (flexibility 10.0 / sqrt(2) = 7.1); linker 0.5 nm as above

presets.name: Primary + secondary antibody (DNA-PAINT docking strand)
presets.notes: Fruh et al. 2021 Table 1, U2OS, DNA on site-specifically labelled secondaries: shell radius 31.8 nm (binder 19.3), FWHM 21.6 nm (flexibility 15.3); the imager's dye at the antibody-proximal end of the docking strand, a C5 linker (about 0.5 nm) from the antibody (Results). Larger than with a dye: the authors suspect partly unfolded DNA-IgG conjugates

presets.name: Labelled primary antibody (DNA-PAINT docking strand)
presets.notes: Fruh et al. 2021 Table 1, human platelets (no U2OS value), DNA on site-specifically labelled primaries: shell radius 23.5 nm (binder 11.0), FWHM 16.7 nm (flexibility 11.8); linker 0.5 nm as above

presets.name: Nanobody (dye)
presets.notes: Mikhaylova et al. 2015: a nanobody is ~15 kDa, ~4 nm; the dye of the anti-tubulin VHH#2 is < 2.5 nm from the lattice (from the microtubule FWHM). The split into binder 1.5 + flexibility 1.0 + linker 0.5 (mean displacement ~2 nm) is an estimate within that bound; Ries et al. 2012: anti-GFP nanobodies, minimal linkage error (no number)

presets.name: Nanobody with a DNA-PAINT docking strand
presets.notes: the nanobody as above; the linker is the docking strand with its bound imager: estimate 1-4 nm (a ~9-10 nt docking strand is ~3 nm as a duplex at 0.34 nm per base pair, the imager's dye at its proximal or distal end, plus spacers). Soeller et al. 2025 image Nup96-mEGFP with anti-GFP nanobody docking strands (no distance given)

presets.name: SNAP / Halo tag (dye or docking strand)
presets.notes: Nieves et al. 2019: SNAP and HaloTag are below 5 nm, one ligand per tag. Estimates within that: binder 2.5 nm (the tag's ligand site about half its size from the fusion point), flexibility 2.0 nm (the fusion linker), linker 0.5-1 nm (the ligand's linker to the dye)

presets.name: Fluorescent protein fusion
presets.notes: the chromophore forms from the central helix inside the beta-barrel (Ormo et al. 1996, Yang et al. 1996): no chemical linker (0 nm, it is part of the protein). Binder 2.0 nm (about half the barrel's length, *estimate*: the dimensions are in the papers' full texts, not checked), flexibility 2.0 nm (the fusion linker, *estimate*)

linkagePresets.notes: Where a label's dye sits relative to its binding site (issue 15; scope/dyes.js linkedDye), in three parts: the binder (the probe: binderNm from the site along the structure's axis -- a microtubule: radially out of the lattice; a pore: its corner's radial direction in the ring plane -- then its flexibility, a uniform ball of radius binderFlexNm), the chemical linker from the probe to the dye (length uniform in volume in [linkerMinNm, linkerMaxNm], direction uniform) and the dye at the end. The antibody presets put the shell centre and width of Fruh et al. 2021 Table 1 on this model (the paper fits a Gaussian ring; the model's radial profile has the same centre and FWHM). The ball can reach into the structure (no excluded volume)

dSTORM.notes: Table 1 (MEA); 405 nm sensitivity '++' (Table 2: >25 % reactivated by 0.25 s at 10-30 W/cm^2, i.e. > ~57 /s per kW/cm^2); initialOnSec (at the reference intensity) estimate.

WideField.notes: estimate (order of magnitude without oxygen scavenging)

dSTORM.notes: estimate: Alexa 532 is not in Dempsey et al. 2011 Table 1; values in the range of its green/yellow dyes (Alexa 488, Atto 520, Cy3B), 405 sensitivity '+'.

DNA-PAINT.notes: k_on: order of magnitude of 9-10 nt imagers (estimate; faster with optimized sequences, schueder2019). onSec 0.05 s keeps the pre-issue-16 default look; 9 nt docking strands bind for ~0.3-1 s.

dyes.name: Cy3B

DNA-PAINT.notes: Cy3b-labeled imager strands (0.6-3 nM, 561 nm TIR; microtubules and DNA origami) in jungmann2014; kinetics as ATTO 655 (estimate: k_on of 9-10 nt imagers, onSec the default look).

dSTORM.notes: Table 1 (MEA: 1,365 photons per cycle, duty cycle 0.0003, 8 switching cycles); 405 nm sensitivity '+' (Table 2); initialOnSec estimate. Its photons per cycle rise with the excitation intensity (Results), which is not modelled (dstormReference notes).

dyes.notes: FPbase has no peak wavelengths for Cy3B: 559/570 nm from dempsey2011 Table 1 (override); its extinction coefficient (130,000) and quantum yield (0.67) are FPbase's, as in that table.

PALM.notes: fluorescent fraction: estimate in the range of durisic2014; ON/OFF/bleach and 405 rate: estimates; primed conversion weak for mEos-type proteins (turkowyd2017; coefficient an estimate).

WideField.notes: the green state as a widefield FP (estimate)

PALM.notes: primed conversion (488 + 730 nm) is efficient for Dendra2 (dempsey2015, turkowyd2017); all rates and the fluorescent fraction are estimates.

dyes.name: Hoechst 33342
dyes.notes: FPbase has no extinction coefficient or quantum yield for Hoechst 33342: eps ~46000 at 350 nm and QY ~0.4 (DNA-bound) are estimates of commonly quoted vendor values, not checked against a source.

dyes.name: Custom (parametric spectra)
dyes.notes: Skewed-Gaussian excitation/emission shapes from the peaks and widths (no FPbase data); every value is the user's to set.
